issues.legal_issue: An acquisition of one property under a composite notice cannot stand when the common expression of urgency relied on to dispense with objections has already been held insufficient.
material_facts: The property was one of fourteen properties covered by a single acquisition notice, which expressed a common opinion that urgency justified taking possession and dispensing with objections.

The same notice was set aside in a challenge concerning another listed property, in part because its expression of urgency was insufficient; the Supreme Court dismissed the challenge to that decision.
The acquisition of the property at issue was set aside by following the decision concerning the other property, and the order dismissing the appeal was challenged by review.
issues.conclusion: The common expression of urgency could not be treated as sufficient for this property after it had been held insufficient for another property covered by the same notice. The order dismissing the appeal was not legally erroneous, and the review application was dismissed without costs.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4, 17(1) and 17(4) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the notice relied on a common expression of urgency to invoke the urgency procedure and dispense with objections. Applying the decision in Banwari Lal & Sons v. Union of India, the Court held that the insufficiency of that common expression was not peculiar to one property: it could not be partly valid and partly invalid across properties covered by the composite notice. The Court did not decide whether the broader principles concerning urgency under Section 17 were correctly stated in Banwari Lal.

predicates.review_of_appeal_dismissal: The applicant sought review of an order dismissing an appeal concerning an acquisition.
predicates.composite_notice_covers_multiple_propert: The acquisition notice covered multiple properties in one notice.
predicates.common_urgency_basis: The notice relied on the same expression of urgency for the properties it covered.
predicates.same_urgency_basis_previously_held_insuf: A court had previously set aside action concerning another property under the same notice because the common expression of urgency was insufficient.

issues.definition: When a review concerns dismissal of an appeal about a property covered by a composite notice, and the notice's common urgency basis has already been held insufficient for another covered property, the review application is dismissed.
